idiom_name: for (x in coll) over iterator(), plus Iterable.forEach and lazy sequences
implementation_notes: Kotlin's for loop over a collection is sugar for the iterator protocol (operator iterator(), hasNext(), next()), and because the operators can be defined by any class the statement works for custom types as well - the collection keeps the walk, the caller writes one line. forEach(action: (T) -> Unit) is the message form for side effects and is inline, so the lambda is not allocated; the transforming messages exist twice, eagerly on Iterable (map/filter/fold) and lazily on Sequence, which produces elements on demand and avoids intermediate collections. Use for/for-in when the body needs break, continue or a non-local return, since forEach cannot exit early.
pitfalls: forEach cannot break: a return@forEach label continues with the next element rather than stopping the walk, so searches need first/find or a for loop.
Iterating a mutable collection while the body mutates it can throw ConcurrentModificationException on fail-fast iterators (ArrayList, HashMap); use removeAll/retainAll or iterate over a snapshot.

asSequence() is lazy and single-use: nothing executes until a terminal operation, exception timing shifts, and a sequence backed by another sequence cannot be traversed twice unless it is constrained once.
